previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma on Cytoxan, COPD, and a history of bladder cancer with neobladder, was admitted with a one-week history of productive cough, shortness of breath, and one day of fever. He had recently seen his oncologist and started levofloxacin, but developed a high fever prompting ED evaluation. He was treated for neutropenic fever and pneumonia with cefepime and levofloxacin. His oxygen requirement improved rapidly, and he was weaned off supplemental oxygen by the first day. Blood cultures remained negative, sputum was contaminated, and viral testing was negative. His neutrophil count recovered, allowing discontinuation of cefepime. A urine culture grew Enterococcus, treated with amoxicillin. His COPD was managed with nebulizers, and symptoms improved. He remained afebrile, stable, and was discharged home on oral levofloxacin and amoxicillin with follow-up arranged.

Brief Hospital Course:
PRIMARY REASON FOR HOSPITALIZATION:
___ with a history of refractory multiple myeloma, recently 
diagnosed MDS with pancytopenia, admitted for hypercalcemia.

ACTIVE DIAGNOSES:
# Hypercalcemia: Patient presented with hypercalcemia with a 
corrected serum calcium level of 13.8. He was symptomatic, with 
mildly altered mental status. While some degree of hypercalcemia 
may be secondary to dehydration, most likely etiology is 
secondary to multiple myeloma with bony osteoclastic activity or 
production of activating factors. Lower suspicion for 
paraneoplastic production of PTHrP or calcitriol production. 
Patient is not on any medications known to cause elevation of 
calcium levels.  Patient was aggressively hydrated first with NS 
and then LR at 200cc/hr, strict ins and outs were monitored.  
Patient was given q12h calcitonin and palmidronate.  Ca levels 
were trended and normalized by time of discharge.

# MDS: Counts stable at baseline. Hct ranging from ___, plts 
___. CBC with diff (and ANC) were trended throughout 
admission.  Patient was transfused for hct<24 and platelets<10.

#CAP: Patient had crackles at lung bases, imaging shows 
pneumonia or pneumonitis at bases, and patient endorses a hx of 
increased sputum production.  He was treated with levofloxacin 
for a 7 day course for CAP.

CHRONIC DIAGNOSES:
# Multiple Myeloma: Patient's Revlimid treatment was put on hold 
during admission. He had no complaints of bony pain, but was 
continued on home pain control regimen of oxycontin 40mg PO 
q12h, gabapentin, and oxycodone prn. IgG changed from 4028 to 
3434.  He was maintained on acyclovir prophylaxis.

# COPD: No evidence of active exacerbation and no current oxygen 
requirement. Patient did complain of cough on admission, so a 
CXR was obtained which revealed pneumonia.  He was continued on 
home maintenance regimen with break through inhalers.

# CAD: History of prior PCI, but not currently on ASA (assumed 
secondary to thrombocytopenia.  He was continued on home 
metoprolol.

# AAA: Last documented size was 5.1cm in ___ and has not had 
imaging since.  Patient will follow-up on this issue as an 
outpatient.

# Depression: Continue home citalopram.

He will follow up with his primary oncologist and was prescribed 
levofloxacin on discharge to finish a 7 day course.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ man with myeloma presenting with cough.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, most recently from ___.

The right lung shows evidence of haziness at the base. In the left lower base
there is an opacity possibly representing an infectious process.  Together
these findings could represent a multifocal pneumonia or aspiration.
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is unremarkable.  There are no pleural effusions.
Hilar contours are unremarkable.  There are no pneumothoraces.

IMPRESSION:  Bilateral lower lobe opacities representative of an infectious
process and/or aspiration.

INDICATION:  Patient with new dyspnea on exertion, to evaluate for
infiltrates.  History of multiple myeloma who is on chemotherapy.

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced MDCT of thorax was performed using a standard
department protocol.  Contiguous axial images at 5-mm and 1.25-mm slice
thickness were reviewed concurrently with coronal and sagittal reformats.

Comparisons were made with prior chest CTs through ___, with the most
recent from ___.

FINDINGS:

LUNGS:  Very minimal secretions are seen in the upper and lower trachea and
bilateral main bronchi.  Bronchial wall thickening is mild.  Centrilobular and
paraseptal emphysema is upper lobe predominant.  Since ___, extent of
bronchial wall thickening and multifocal centrilobular opacities with tree in
___ pattern suggesting bronchiolitis has worsened. Minimal right and traceleft
pleural effusions, focal parenchymal opacity in the superior segment of the
both lower lobe and posterior segment of the right upper lobe which are likely
secondary to aspiration and bilateral mild dependent lung atelectasis are new.


MEDIASTINUM:  Thyroid gland is normal.  Multiple lymph nodes are seen in the
mediastinum but none of them meet the CT size criteria for pathological
enlargement.  When compared to the prior CT dated ___, all these
lymph nodes have minimally increased in size; for example, a 7.3-mm precarinal
lymph node was previously 5 mm.  There are no pathologically enlarged central
mediastinal, supraclavicular, or axillary lymph nodes.  Heart is normal size
without pericardial effusion.  Low-density cardia suggests anemia. 
Atherosclerotic calcification involving the coronary arteries is moderate to
severe.  Minimal fluid in the anterior pericardial space is unchanged since
___.

ABDOMEN:  The study is not tailored for evaluation of abdomen; however,
limited views were remarkable only to reveal high-density GB content
suggestive of sludge in a partially distended gallbladder and pericholecystic
and mesenteric fat stranding.  Moderate to severe atherosclerotic
calcification seen in the imaged portion of abdominal aorta. Hital Hernia is
mild and stable.  Both adrenal glands are normal.

BONES:  Mild wedge compression fractures of D7, D8 vertebrae have been stable.
Degenerative changes are seen at multiple thoracic vertebral levels.  There is
no bone lesion suspicious for malignancy/infection.


IMPRESSION:

1.  Since ___ Bilateral, multifocal lower lobe predominant bronchiolitis
and diffuse bronchial wall thickening suggesting active infection has
worsened.

2.  Since ___, minimal right and trace left pleural effusions, bilateral
lower lobe superior segment and posterior segment of right upper lobe
opacities likely aspiration,  minimal dependent lung atelectasis in both lower
lobes are new.

3.  Partially distended GB filled with sludge and minimal pericholecystic and
mesenteric fat stranding.  Ultrasound abdomen is suggested for further
evaluation.
